title: Uncover silent Redis backpressure during ingress surges; add trace enrichment & runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a capacity surge on 2026-02-16 the console experienced a prolonged degradation in per-tenant tail latency visibility. The incident postmortem showed that our Redis-backed ingress meter began applying backpressure silently: metrics emitted from the metric-ingest service were being dropped or delayed without a clear enum of failure modes. Dashboards showed normal ingest rates while queue lengths and downstream latency climbed. Traces recovered from sampled requests lacked correlation IDs through the ingest -> router -> runtime handoff, making it hard to attribute which tenants were affected.

What failed: (1) Missing per-tenant queue-depth and per-route queue-age metrics at high cardinality; (2) dashboard panels used aggregate metrics that masked skewed tails; (3) tracing sampling and baggage propagation dropped critical correlation keys at the metric-ingest boundary; (4) Redis client library retried/backoff behavior suppressed observable errors and produced misleading success counts.

Hypothesis: A combination of a short maintenance window for Redis (restarts + slow eviction), an update to our Redis client that switched error handling to "best-effort", and a dashboard query that used mean/95p instead of tail histograms allowed the failure to remain invisible until customer-facing latency increased.

Goal: Restore deterministic visibility for capacity-sensitive signals (per-tenant queue depth/age, redis circuit/open counts, trace correlation ids) and ship a playbook + runbook to detect and mitigate silent backpressure within 2 sprint cycles.
action_items: (Miguel) Add high-cardinality per-tenant queue_depth & queue_age gauges in metric-ingest (prometheus histogram + exemplar) and emit tenant_id as label
(Aisha) Create enriched trace spans at ingest->router boundary that include correlation_id and tenant_id; bump trace sampling to preserve 1% of ingress under load
(Infra) Instrument Redis client library to expose circuit state and retry counters to Prometheus (owner: Priya Desai)
(Observability) Replace aggregate 'ingest_rate' panels with tail-aware panels (p99/p999 histograms + heatmap) and add an alert for sustained tail growth (owner: Jin Wu)
(SRE) Add dashboard-driven chaos tests that simulate Redis latency and eviction patterns in staging (owner: Elena Korhonen)

(All) Draft an incident runbook section for 'silent backpressure' with immediate mitigation steps (throttle policies, fallback to cached responses, fail-open thresholds) and link to the postmortem (owner: Miguel)
(PM) Coordinate release notes and customer communications template for tenants that might see tail latency during rollout (owner: Noah Kim)
comments: 2026-02-18 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem review. Initial instrumentation gaps identified from trace sampling artifacts and dashboard queries. Adding owners to action items.

2026-02-20 Miguel Ramos: Pushed spike PR to add tenant_id label to queue_depth (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metric-ingest/pull/482). Running local load test to validate cardinality impact.

2026-02-22 Jin Wu: Drafted new dashboard panels and alert queries; put on staging dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/staging/ingest-tail-visibility. Alert thresholds proposal posted in thread.

2026-02-25 Priya Desai: Instrumented redis client metrics in a feature branch and added circuit_open_count + retry_total counters (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-redis-telemetry/pull/19). Observed increased metric churn during synthetic eviction test.

2026-03-01 Elena Korhonen: Staging chaos test shows that adding 200ms median Redis latency surfaces p999 tail in new panels; existing aggregate panels still look normal. Filed follow-up to throttle_backpressure feature (ENG-99912).

2026-03-03 Miguel Ramos: Consolidated runbook draft in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Silent+Backpressure+Runbook. Requesting review from SRE and Observability owners before rollout.
